title.narrative: HOPE PROJECT: Nicaraguan forced displacement and migration in Costa Rica

description.narrative: The Overall Objective (Impact) of this action is: ¿Enhanced socioeconomic integration and social cohesion of Nicaraguan forcibly displaced persons and economic migrants in Costa Rica¿.The Specific(s) Objectives (SO) / Outcomes of this Action are:     SO 1: Improve regularization process of Nicaraguan forcibly displaced persons and migrants in Costa Rica to ensure effective access to basic rights and services. SO 2: Enhance economic inclusion and social cohesion of forcibly displaced persons, migrants and hosting communities in Costa Rica with a particular focus on women and youth in vulnerable situationsWithin the flexibility of a MIP designed for a fragile context and in direct response to a recent phenomenon, the EU Delegation proposes an Action to address the recent migration wave driven by political repression, and economic consequences. This situation has led thousands of Nicaraguans to seek refugee or better economic opportunities abroad, mainly in Costa Rica and the United States. This  Action proposes support the government of Costa Rica in its efforts to manage the recent surge of Nicaraguan migrants in a transparent and responsible way, as well as complement efforts of key partners in the region, including Spain, Luxemburg, and the USA among others. Since the political crisis of 2018 as well as the impact of of coronavirus pandemic and recurrent natural disasters (such as hurricanes ETA et IOTA (2020) and the El Niño phenomenon) have resulted in forced displacement and a migration crisis as well as an economic crisis. This crisis led to a dramatic increase in the number of Nicaraguans seeking protection, asylum, as well as to improve their living conditions outside their country.Costa Rica has emerged as the fourth-largest recipient country globally for new individual asylum applications during the years 2021 and 2022. This influx has strained the capacity of the organizations providing assistance to asylum seekers and the relevant government agencies. According to UNHCR in Costa Rica, Nicaraguans constituted 88% of the total requests for refugee status in 2023. With over 200,000 individuals awaiting the processing of their asylum applications, asylum seekers and refugees now constitute more than 4% of the national population. This percentage represents the highest proportion in the region, surpassing that of Colombia and Ecuador, both standing at approximately 3%.
